candidates.exact_span: Select only those Elements and Sections which apply to your sludge reuse or disposal practice.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a given facility's sludge practice falls under Element 1, 2, or 3 (and which sections within an element) determines which monitoring and reporting obligations are in scope for FY2025 and whether missing or absent DMR data should be treated as a conditional non-requirement versus an unresolved gap.

candidates.exact_span: If your facility utilizes more than one type of disposal or reuse method (for example, Element I and Element II apply) or the quality of your sludge varies (for example, Section II and Section III of Element I apply) use a separate Discharge Monitoring Report (DMR) for each Section that is applicable.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether multiple disposal methods or sludge-quality classes coexist at a facility changes how many distinct DMR obligations exist and how reported or missing evidence should be mapped to each applicable section during FY2025 evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: The sludge DMRs shall be due by February 19th of each year and shall cover the previous January through December time period. (The sludge DMRs for permits in Texas shall be due by September 1 of each year, with the reporting period of August 1 to July 31)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The applicable due date and January–December versus August–July reporting window determine which monitoring periods intersect Federal FY2025 and whether a missing or late DMR reflects an unmet obligation or falls outside the evaluated period.

candidates.exact_span: The sludge conditions do not apply to wastewater treatment lagoons where sludge is not wasted for final reuse/disposal.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a lagoon facility wastes sludge for final reuse or disposal governs whether Part IV sludge conditions—including any associated numeric limits and DMR requirements—are applicable at all, versus being excluded from limit comparison, monitoring obligation, and missing-evidence analysis.

candidates.exact_span: If the sludge is not removed, the permittee shall indicate on the DMR "No Discharge".
candidates.computation_change_reason: When sludge is not removed, this establishes a specific documented reporting response ('No Discharge') rather than an ordinary numeric result; misclassifying that indication affects whether monitoring was required and whether missing data represents a documented no-data state versus inadequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span:
SECTION II:          Page 6 - Requirements Specific to Bulk Sewage Sludge for Application to the Land
                     Meeting Class A or B Pathogen Reduction and the Cumulative Loading Rates in

candidates.computation_change_reason: Section II applies under alternative combinations of pathogen class and Table 2 cumulative loading rates versus Table 3 pollutant concentrations; different readings of which branch applies change which enforceable numeric limits and monitoring requirements are in effect.

candidates.exact_span:

                     Concentrations in Table 3 and Class A Pathogen Reduction Requirements
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applicability hinges on simultaneous satisfaction of Table 3 pollutant concentrations and Class A pathogen reduction; whether a facility's sludge meets both conditions determines if Section III limits and obligations apply instead of Section II or IV.

candidates.exact_span:
SECTION IV:           Page 12 - Requirements Specific to Sludge Sold or Given Away in a Bag or Other
                     Container for Application to the Land that does not meet the Pollutant Concentrations
                     in Table 3
candidates.computation_change_reason: Section IV is triggered only for bagged or containerized sludge distributed for land application that fails Table 3 pollutant concentrations; interpreting disposal method and Table 3 compliance differently changes which numeric limits and monitoring rules govern the facility.

candidates.exact_span:
SECTION II:          Page 19 - Requirements Specific to Surface Disposal Sites Without a Liner and
                     Leachate Collection System
candidates.computation_change_reason: Surface disposal obligations under Element 2 split by liner and leachate-collection presence; classifying a site as without those controls versus with them (Section III) changes which enforceable limits and monitoring requirements apply.

candidates.exact_span:
SECTION III:         Page 20 - Requirements Specific to Surface Disposal Sites With a Liner and Leachate
                     Collection System
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applicability of this section depends on whether the surface disposal site has both a liner and a leachate collection system; that site-characterization choice determines which numeric limits and monitoring duties replace those under Section II.
